memory_candidates.content: The harness's `paths:` frontmatter auto-load mechanism (rules with a `paths:` glob in their YAML frontmatter) fires ONLY on the Read/Edit/Write tool family -- it never fires for a Bash command, even one whose argument string names or `cat`s a matching path. This was verified via a live minimal-pair test (identical file/content exposure, differing only in tool). Consequence for any rule intended to guard a Bash-invoked command (e.g. a build tool like `latexmk`/`pdflatex`): a paths-glob-only rule cannot reach an agent that issues the guarded Bash command without ever touching a matching path via Read/Edit/Write first. The reliable complement is an eager, task-type-independent pointer (e.g. in the extension's CLAUDE.md merge source / EXTENSION.md), which is unconditionally in the session prefix whenever the extension is loaded, with no trigger dependency at all.
